the chemical denervation by 5, 6-DHT is accompanied by the appearance of large numbers of highly fluorescent axons provided by numerous intensely fluorescent swellings, resembling the proximal stumps and droplets of mechanically severed axons.

In summary, our research is concerned with
an analysis of the morphological and biochemical changes in the rat brain induced by a single intraventralic injection of 75μg of 5,6-dihtroxytryptamine per animal.
the demonstration of the chemical and morphological changes induced by 5-hydroxylated tryptamine derivatives in the central indoleamine neurons of the rat.

the demonstration of a degeneration of varicose serotonin containing nerve endings in the rat brain induced by a single intraventri- cular administration of 75 μ g 5,6- dihydroxytryptamine per animal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 5,6-hydroxytrytpamine induced “chemical” degeneration of indolamine containing nerve terminals is a highly selective process, which does not involve the destruction of the cell bodies of serotonin containing neurons.
5,6-dihtoxytryptamine is a powerful neurotoxin for indoleamine containing neurons in the CNS of the rat.

5,6 DHT, when injected into the ventricular system, induces a degeneration of serotonin and/or indoleamine containing terminals of neurons in the rat brain, which is characterized by a pronounced loss of yellow fluorescent axonal varicosities, by a significant drop in the amount of 5-hydroxv-tryptamine and in the number of indoleamine storing synaptic vesicles and by the presence of swollen, highly fluorescent axonal stumps.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

5,6 DHT, a potent and highly selective neurotoxin for serotonin containing neurons, induces a chemical degeneration of these neurons in the rat brain, which is reflected in a number of morphological and biochemical parameters, and which is accompanied by the formation of numerous axonal swellings (“droplet” formation) of indoleamine axons, which are provided with a high content of indoleamine fluorescent material and are in a process of degeneration.

the chemical lesioning of indoleamine terminals in the rat CNS by 5, 6-DHT is not a mere inhibition of the serotonin synthesis and storage, but rather a degeneration of serotonin containing axons and their terminals.

5,6- DHT induces a chemical lesion of the indoleamine containing terminals of serotonin containing neurons, and this lesion is accompanied by the release of indoleamine from the terminals, which can be detected as an accumulation of indoleamine fluorescence in the pericarya of these neurons, and as an accumulation of 5-hydroxtryptamine in the brain tissue.
